1193	// errUnreachablePathLink is the refusal reason for a registry path that runs
1194	// into a symbolic link whose target cannot be resolved — a dangling link or a
1195	// link loop, on a directory component as well as on the final component. It
1196	// is deliberately worded as an unusable link, not as a registry file that has
1197	// merely not been created: the two are indistinguishable from ReadFile's
1198	// fs.ErrNotExist alone, and only the former is a first registration.
1199	var errUnreachablePathLink = errors.New("a symbolic link in the registry path has a target that does not exist or cannot be resolved")
1200	
1201	// checkRegistryPathReachable decides, before the registry bytes are read,
1202	// whether path can reach anything the way the kernel resolves names. It
1203	// exists because os.ReadFile reports fs.ErrNotExist both for a registry file
1204	// that has never been created (a legitimate first registration) and for a
1205	// path that descends through a dangling directory symbolic link (not one):
1206	// with work/alias pointing at a missing directory, ReadFile on
1207	// work/alias/batches.json — and, because the kernel cannot step ".." out of
1208	// a directory the link never reaches, on work/alias/../batches.json too —
1209	// returns exactly the not-exist error even when work/batches.json exists.
1210	//
1211	// The check climbs through the raw components missing from the filesystem
1212	// (never by lexical cleaning, which would collapse "alias/.." before the
1213	// kernel resolves alias) to the longest existing prefix. A ".." among the
1214	// missing components is harmless here: without a symbolic link in the path
1215	// the prefix genuinely exists, so such a path is either a real file (read
1216	// normally) or a path through missing ordinary directories, and reading is
1217	// allowed either way — the read creates nothing and Save runs its own
1218	// stricter refusal before writing. What must fail is an existing prefix that
1219	// is itself a symbolic link which cannot be chased to a real directory:
1220	// EvalSymlinks on the prefix names exactly that failure for a dangling
1221	// link or a link loop, including one reached through several links. A
1222	// relative link target is resolved by EvalSymlinks against the link's own
1223	// directory, matching the kernel. The check only calls Lstat and
1224	// EvalSymlinks, so it never creates a directory, registry file or temporary
1225	// file and never modifies a link.
1226	func checkRegistryPathReachable(path string) error {
1227		cur := path
1228		for {
1229			info, err := os.Lstat(cur)
1230			if err == nil {
1231				// cur is the longest existing prefix. A prefix that is itself a
1232				// symbolic link which cannot be chased to a real directory is the
1233				// one failure that looks like a never-created registry file: the
1234				// final read reports fs.ErrNotExist either way. EvalSymlinks
1235				// resolves an absolute link target, or a relative one against the
1236				// link's own directory (never the process working directory),
1237				// through every hop of a chain; a dangling link or a loop fails
1238				// here. Any other failure at a deeper component (for example
1239				// permission denied) is left for the read itself to report.
1240				if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
1241					if _, eerr := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cur); eerr != nil {
1242						return errUnreachablePathLink
1243					}
1244				}
1245				return nil
1246			}
1247			parent, _ := rawParent(cur)
1248			if parent == cur {
1249				// No existing prefix at all: a bare relative name resolved
1250				// against the process working directory, the same way an
1251				// ordinary open would. No symbolic link could have been
1252				// encountered, so a not-exist is an ordinary first registration
1253				// and any other failure is the read's own to report.
1254				return nil
1255			}
1256			cur = parent
1257		}
1258	}

1260	// resolveRegistryTarget returns the real file a save to path must replace,
1261	// resolved the same way the kernel resolves path for reads: every symbolic
1262	// link is chased — links on DIRECTORY components included — and every ".."
1263	// steps out of the directory it really leaves, not out of the link's own
1264	// parent name. The result is a cleaned path with no link or ".." component
1265	// naming exactly the file Load read, so the temporary file and the rename
1266	// land in the target's real directory (a relative path stays relative,
1267	// resolved against the process working directory as the input was).
1268	//
1269	// Physical resolution is what keeps read and save locations identical when a
1270	// directory link is followed by "..": with work/alias -> store/child, the
1271	// path work/alias/../batches.json means store/batches.json. Lexical cleaning
1272	// (filepath.Clean, filepath.Dir) collapses alias/.. to work and would save
1273	// next to the link — into an unrelated, possibly read-only directory.
1274	// Components missing from the filesystem (a first registration) are appended
1275	// verbatim onto the longest existing prefix, so creating a new file needs
1276	// write permission only in the directory that really holds it.
1277	//
1278	// A path that descends into a directory that does not exist and only then
1279	// climbs back with ".." — store/missing/../batches.json with no store/missing
1280	// — cannot reach any file the way the kernel resolves names, so it is an
1281	// error rather than a first registration: the save neither creates the
1282	// missing directory (which would turn an unresolvable path into a live one)
1283	// nor writes the lexically cleaned name (store/batches.json), which may be an
1284	// unrelated existing registry. A path that only creates new directories
1285	// without climbing back out (store/new/batches.json), or climbs ".." after a
1286	// prefix that really exists, is resolved and saved normally.
1287	//
1288	// A dangling symbolic link or a link loop — on the final component or on a
1289	// directory leading to it — is an error: the save must not create the target
1290	// or overwrite the link as if this were a first registration.
1291	func resolveRegistryTarget(path string) (string, error) {
1292		// Climb through components missing from the filesystem by stripping raw
1293		// path segments, never by lexical cleaning: filepath.Clean would collapse
1294		// "alias/.." against the link's own parent name before the kernel ever
1295		// resolves alias, sending the save at work/x.json instead of store/x.json.
1296		// os.Lstat resolves every component but the last exactly as the kernel
1297		// does, so each surviving prefix is checked with its real meaning.
1298		cur := path
1299		var tail []string
1300		for {
1301			info, err := os.Lstat(cur)
1302			if err == nil {
1303				// Refuse a ".." among the not-yet-existing components that climbs
1304				// back out of a directory which would first have to be created:
1305				// the user's path itself cannot name anything there, and creating
1306				// the directory would make a previously unresolvable path valid.
1307				if missing, escape := missingDirDotDotEscape(tail); escape {
1308					return "", errEscapeThroughMissingDir(missing)
1309				}
1310				// cur is the longest existing prefix. Resolve it physically: an
1311				// absolute link target, or a relative one resolved against the
1312				// link's own directory (never the process working directory), is
1313				// followed; a dangling link or a loop fails here and is reported
1314				// as an unusable symbolic link rather than a fresh-registry path.
1315				base, eerr := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cur)
1316				if eerr != nil {
1317					if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
1318						return "", fmt.Errorf("registry path is a symbolic link whose target cannot be resolved: %w", eerr)
1319					}
1320					return "", fmt.Errorf("cannot inspect registry path: %w", eerr)
1321				}
1322				// Append the not-yet-existing components verbatim: a first
1323				// registration needs write permission only in the real directory
1324				// that will hold the file, never in directories merely traversed.
1325				target := base
1326				for i := len(tail) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
1327					target = filepath.Join(target, tail[i])
1328				}
1329				return filepath.Clean(target), nil
1330			}
1331			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
1332				return "", fmt.Errorf("cannot inspect registry path: %w", err)
1333			}
1334			parent, base := rawParent(cur)
1335			tail = append(tail, base)
1336			if parent == cur {
1337				// A bare relative name with no existing prefix: it names a file
1338				// in the process working directory, just as a plain open would —
1339				// unless it climbs ".." out of a directory that does not exist.
1340				if missing, escape := missingDirDotDotEscape(tail); escape {
1341					return "", errEscapeThroughMissingDir(missing)
1342				}
1343				return filepath.Clean(path), nil
1344			}
1345			cur = parent
1346		}
1347	}
1348	
1349	// missingDirDotDotEscape inspects the raw components stripped while climbing
1350	// to the longest existing prefix. tail holds them from the registry file end
1351	// (tail[0] is the final, registry-file component) toward the existing prefix
1352	// (tail[len-1] sits next to it). A ".." that climbs out of a directory
1353	// descended into only within the not-yet-existing tail marks exactly the
1354	// unresolvable shape — store/missing/../batches.json — that must be refused:
1355	// the kernel cannot resolve the ".." until "missing" exists, and it never
1356	// legitimately exists on this path.
1357	//
1358	// The final component is the registry file name, never a directory descent,
1359	// so tail[0] is not counted. ".." steps matched by an equally non-existent
1360	// descent keep the lexical depth positive and do not cancel the violation:
1361	// the first ".." that leaves a missing directory is already fatal. The
1362	// returned name is the missing directory that ".." immediately tries to
1363	// leave. Symlinked or genuinely existing components never reach tail, so
1364	// this never trips over a physical ".." (as after work/alias -> store/child).
1365	func missingDirDotDotEscape(tail []string) (missing string, escape bool) {
1366		depth := 0
1367		lastMissing := ""
1368		// Walk from the existing-prefix side toward the file.
1369		for i := len(tail) - 1; i >= 1; i-- {
1370			switch tail[i] {
1371			case ".", "":
1372				// A "." (or the empty segment of a doubled separator) is a
1373				// lexical no-op even in the not-yet-existing tail.
1374			case "..":
1375				if depth > 0 {
1376					return lastMissing, true
1377				}
1378				depth--
1379			default:
1380				depth++
1381				lastMissing = tail[i]
1382			}
1383		}
1384		return "", false
1385	}
1386	
1387	// errEscapeThroughMissingDir is the refusal reason for a registry path that
1388	// descends into a non-existent directory and then climbs back with "..". The
1389	// Save wrapper adds the user-supplied path; the missing directory is named so
1390	// the user can see which component made the path unresolvable.
1391	func errEscapeThroughMissingDir(missing string) error {
1392		return fmt.Errorf(
1393			"the path descends through directory %s, which does not exist, and then climbs back with \"..\"; "+
1394				"such a path cannot reach an existing file and the missing directory is not created to make it valid, so the registry is not written",
1395			strconv.Quote(missing))
1396	}
1397	
1398	// rawParent splits path at its final separator without resolving "..", so the
1399	// caller can climb one raw component at a time and keep physical resolution of
1400	// any directory link in the surviving prefix.
1401	func rawParent(path string) (parent, base string) {
1402		i := strings.LastIndexByte(path, os.PathSeparator)
1403		if i < 0 {
1404			return path, path
1405		}
1406		return path[:i], path[i+1:]
1407	}

1409	// Save atomically writes reg to path, replacing the file only after the new
1410	// content is fully on disk so an existing registry stays usable on failure.
1411	// Records are serialized in their current order; the file is created with
1412	// 0644 permissions or, when replacing an existing file, with its permissions.
1413	//
1414	// When path reaches the registry through a symbolic link, the link's target
1415	// is the file replaced: the new content is prepared next to the target and
1416	// moved over it, so the link stays a link to the same target and the target
1417	// keeps its permissions, while reads through either the link or the real
1418	// path see the saved records. This holds for a link on the final component
1419	// and for a link on a DIRECTORY component, including a ".." that steps back
1420	// after it: with work/alias -> store/child, work/alias/../batches.json is
1421	// store/batches.json, and the save writes there even though the directory
1422	// containing the link (here work) is not writable — write access is needed
1423	// only in the target's real directory. A link whose target does not exist,
1424	// or a link loop, on the file or on a leading directory, rejects the save
1425	// with an error naming path — the target is never created and the link is
1426	// never replaced.
1427	//
1428	// A path that descends through a directory that does not exist and only then
1429	// climbs back with ".." (store/missing/../batches.json with store/missing
1430	// absent) is likewise rejected before anything is written: such a path
1431	// reaches no file the way the kernel resolves names, so the save neither
1432	// creates the missing directory — which would turn the unresolvable path into
1433	// a live one — nor writes the lexically cleaned name, where an unrelated
1434	// registry could be overwritten. A ".." after a directory that genuinely
1435	// exists, including the real target of a directory symlink, still resolves by
1436	// real directory relations, and a not-yet-existing parent that is never
1437	// climbed out of (store/new/batches.json) is created as on any first save.
1438	//
1439	// A path spelled as a DIRECTORY location — one ending in one or more path
1440	// separators ("store/new.json/"), or whose final component is "." or ".."
1441	// ("store/new/.", "store/new/..") — is rejected with a *DirectoryPathError
1442	// purely on the spelling, before validation or any filesystem change. The
1443	// rule is the same whether the location does not exist yet, already is a
1444	// directory, or has a regular file directly beneath the spelled name: the
1445	// save never creates a missing parent, never writes a registry file or
1446	// temporary file at the name left after stripping the trailing separator or
1447	// the final "."/"..", and never replaces an existing directory or symbolic
1448	// link. Stripping the marker would otherwise create a file the supplied path
1449	// cannot read back ("store/new.json/" would create plain file
1450	// "store/new.json"; "store/new/." would create plain file "store/new"). A
1451	// "." or ".." in a MIDDLE component is not a directory marker and keeps its
1452	// ordinary resolution.
1453	//
1454	// Every record must satisfy the same effective-value rules Load enforces, so
1455	// a registry saved successfully always reads back: batch, product and unit
1456	// must be non-empty valid UTF-8 text (kept verbatim — no trimming or case
1457	// folding, so whitespace-only text is ordinary non-empty text), quantity
1458	// must lie in 1..MaxQuantity, and batch ids must be unique under exact
1459	// byte-for-byte comparison, two identical records included. Any violation
1460	// rejects the whole save before anything is written: an existing target
1461	// keeps its bytes and modification time, a missing target stays missing and
1462	// no temporary file is left behind. A nil or empty Batches is a legal empty
1463	// registry and is written as "batches": [] without touching reg itself.
1464	func Save(path string, reg *Registry) error {
1465		// The path's file-or-directory meaning is decided before anything else: a
1466		// trailing separator or a final "."/".." component spells a directory
1467		// location and can never hold a registry file. Refusing here — purely on
1468		// the spelling, before version and record validation, directory creation,
1469		// the temporary file or the rename — guarantees the table the caller
1470		// handed in is untouched and nothing appears at the name left after
1471		// stripping the trailing directory marker.
1472		if registryPathDenotesDirectory(path) {
1473			return &DirectoryPathError{Path: path}
1474		}
1475		if reg.Version != FormatVersion {
1476			return fmt.Errorf("cannot write registry format version %d", reg.Version)
1477		}
1478		if err := validateForSave(reg); err != nil {
1479			return fmt.Errorf("cannot save registry %q: %w", path, err)
1480		}
1481		target, err := resolveRegistryTarget(path)
1482		if err != nil {
1483			return fmt.Errorf("cannot save registry %q: %w", path, err)
1484		}
1485		mode := os.FileMode(0o644)
1486		if info, err := os.Stat(target); err == nil {
1487			mode = info.Mode().Perm()
1488		} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
1489			return fmt.Errorf("cannot inspect registry %q: %w", path, err)
1490		}
1491	
1492		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(target), 0o755); err != nil {
1493			return fmt.Errorf("cannot save registry %q: %w", path, err)
1494		}
1495	
1496		// Encode a shallow copy so a nil Batches marshals as [] (null would not
1497		// read back) without mutating the caller's registry.
1498		out := *reg
1499		if out.Batches == nil {
1500			out.Batches = []Batch{}
1501		}
1502		var buf bytes.Buffer
1503		enc := json.NewEncoder(&buf)
1504		enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
1505		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
1506		if err := enc.Encode(&out); err != nil {
1507			return fmt.Errorf("cannot encode registry %q: %w", path, err)
1508		}
1509	
1510		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(target), ".govflow-registry-*.tmp")
1511		if err != nil {
1512			return fmt.Errorf("cannot save registry %q: %w", path, err)
1513		}
1514		tmpName := tmp.Name()
1515		abort := func(cause error) error {
1516			tmp.Close()
1517			os.Remove(tmpName)
1518			return fmt.Errorf("cannot save registry %q: %w", path, cause)
1519		}
1520		if _, err := WriteTempContent(tmp, buf.Bytes()); err != nil {
1521			return abort(err)
1522		}
1523		if err := tmp.Chmod(mode); err != nil {
1524			return abort(err)
1525		}
1526		if err := tmp.Sync(); err != nil {
1527			return abort(err)
1528		}
1529		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
1530			os.Remove(tmpName)
1531			return fmt.Errorf("cannot save registry %q: %w", path, err)
1532		}
1533		if err := RenameTempFile(tmpName, target); err != nil {
1534			os.Remove(tmpName)
1535			return fmt.Errorf("cannot save registry %q: %w", path, err)
1536		}
1537		return nil
1538	}

202	func runBatchRegister(args []string, stdout io.Writer) error {
203		fs := flag.NewFlagSet("batch-register", flag.ContinueOnError)
204		fs.SetOutput(io.Discard)
205		registryPath := fs.String("registry", "", "registry `file` to read and write")
206		batchRaw := fs.String("batch", "", "batch number (unique within the registry)")
207		productRaw := fs.String("product", "", "product number")
208		quantityRaw := fs.String("quantity", "", "positive decimal integer quantity")
209		unitRaw := fs.String("unit", "", "measurement unit")
210		if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
211			if errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {
212				fmt.Fprint(stdout, rootUsage())
213				return nil
214			}
215			return &usageError{msg: "batch-register: " + err.Error(), usage: batchRegisterUsage}
216		}
217		if fs.NArg() != 0 {
218			return &usageError{
219				msg:   fmt.Sprintf("batch-register: unexpected positional argument(s): %s", strings.Join(fs.Args(), " ")),
220				usage: batchRegisterUsage,
221			}
222		}
223	
224		// Missing or malformed input must never create or modify the registry
225		// file, so required flags are checked before reading or writing anything.
226		required := []struct {
227			name  string
228			value string
229		}{
230			{"--registry", *registryPath},
231			{"--batch", *batchRaw},
232			{"--product", *productRaw},
233			{"--quantity", *quantityRaw},
234			{"--unit", *unitRaw},
235		}
236		var missing []string
237		for _, f := range required {
238			if f.value == "" {
239				missing = append(missing, f.name)
240			}
241		}
242		if len(missing) > 0 {
243			return &usageError{
244				msg:   "batch-register: missing required flag(s): " + strings.Join(missing, ", "),
245				usage: batchRegisterUsage,
246			}
247		}
248	
249		batch, err := batchreg.NormalizeField(*batchRaw)
250		if err != nil {
251			return &usageError{msg: "batch-register: invalid --batch: " + err.Error(), usage: batchRegisterUsage}
252		}
253		product, err := batchreg.NormalizeField(*productRaw)
254		if err != nil {
255			return &usageError{msg: "batch-register: invalid --product: " + err.Error(), usage: batchRegisterUsage}
256		}
257		unit, err := batchreg.NormalizeField(*unitRaw)
258		if err != nil {
259			return &usageError{msg: "batch-register: invalid --unit: " + err.Error(), usage: batchRegisterUsage}
260		}
261		quantity, err := batchreg.ParseQuantity(*quantityRaw)
262		if err != nil {
263			return &usageError{msg: "batch-register: invalid --quantity: " + err.Error(), usage: batchRegisterUsage}
264		}
265	
266		reg, existed, err := batchreg.Load(*registryPath)
267		if err != nil {
268			return err
269		}
270		outcome, err := batchreg.Register(reg, batchreg.Input{
271			Batch: batch, Product: product, Quantity: quantity, Unit: unit,
272		})
273		if err != nil {
274			return err
275		}
276		if outcome.Created {
277			if err := batchreg.Save(*registryPath, reg); err != nil {
278				if !existed {
279					// Nothing was registered before; drop any partial new file.
280					removePartialNewRegistry(*registryPath)
281				}
282				return err
283			}
284		}
285	
286		status := "duplicate"
287		if outcome.Created {
288			status = "created"
289		}
290		result := struct {
291			Batch    string `json:"batch"`
292			Product  string `json:"product"`
293			Quantity int64  `json:"quantity"`
294			Unit     string `json:"unit"`
295			Status   string `json:"status"`
296		}{
297			Batch:    outcome.Batch.Batch,
298			Product:  outcome.Batch.Product,
299			Quantity: outcome.Batch.Quantity,
300			Unit:     outcome.Batch.Unit,
301			Status:   status,
302		}
303		payload, err := json.Marshal(result)
304		if err != nil {
305			return err
306		}
307		_, err = fmt.Fprintln(stdout, string(payload))
308		return err
309	}

311	func runBatchImport(args []string, stdout io.Writer) error {
312		fs := flag.NewFlagSet("batch-import", flag.ContinueOnError)
313		fs.SetOutput(io.Discard)
314		registryPath := fs.String("registry", "", "registry `file` to read and write")
315		inputPath := fs.String("input", "", "read-only JSON manifest `file` to import")
316		if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
317			if errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {
318				fmt.Fprint(stdout, rootUsage())
319				return nil
320			}
321			return &usageError{msg: "batch-import: " + err.Error(), usage: batchImportUsage}
322		}
323		if fs.NArg() != 0 {
324			return &usageError{
325				msg:   fmt.Sprintf("batch-import: unexpected positional argument(s): %s", strings.Join(fs.Args(), " ")),
326				usage: batchImportUsage,
327			}
328		}
329		if *registryPath == "" || *inputPath == "" {
330			var missing []string
331			if *registryPath == "" {
332				missing = append(missing, "--registry")
333			}
334			if *inputPath == "" {
335				missing = append(missing, "--input")
336			}
337			return &usageError{
338				msg:   "batch-import: missing required flag(s): " + strings.Join(missing, ", "),
339				usage: batchImportUsage,
340			}
341		}
342	
343		// The manifest is read-only and is parsed (and fully validated) before
344		// the registry is loaded or written, so bad input cannot touch it.
345		data, err := os.ReadFile(*inputPath)
346		if err != nil {
347			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: cannot read input file %q: %w", *inputPath, err)
348		}
349		inputs, err := batchreg.ParseManifest(data)
350		if err != nil {
351			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: invalid input file %q: %w", *inputPath, err)
352		}
353	
354		reg, existed, err := batchreg.Load(*registryPath)
355		if err != nil {
356			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: %w", err)
357		}
358		outcomes, err := batchreg.Import(reg, inputs)
359		if err != nil {
360			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: %w", err)
361		}
362	
363		type importResultJSON struct {
364			Batch    string `json:"batch"`
365			Product  string `json:"product"`
366			Quantity int64  `json:"quantity"`
367			Unit     string `json:"unit"`
368			Status   string `json:"status"`
369		}
370		results := make([]importResultJSON, len(outcomes))
371		anyCreated := false
372		for i, o := range outcomes {
373			status := "duplicate"
374			if o.Created {
375				status = "created"
376				anyCreated = true
377			}
378			results[i] = importResultJSON{
379				Batch:    o.Batch.Batch,
380				Product:  o.Batch.Product,
381				Quantity: o.Batch.Quantity,
382				Unit:     o.Batch.Unit,
383				Status:   status,
384			}
385		}
386	
387		// An all-duplicate manifest must leave bytes and mtime untouched, so the
388		// registry is written only when at least one record was newly created.
389		if anyCreated {
390			if err := batchreg.Save(*registryPath, reg); err != nil {
391				if !existed {
392					// The registry never existed before this import; drop any
393					// partial new file so a failed save leaves nothing behind.
394					removePartialNewRegistry(*registryPath)
395				}
396				return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: %w", err)
397			}
398		}
399	
400		payload, err := json.Marshal(struct {
401			Results []importResultJSON `json:"results"`
402		}{Results: results})
403		if err != nil {
404			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: %w", err)
405		}
406		_, err = fmt.Fprintln(stdout, string(payload))
407		if err != nil {
408			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: %w", err)
409		}
410		return nil
411	}
412	
413	// removePartialNewRegistry drops a partially written new registry file after
414	// a failed first save. A symbolic link is never removed: the link is the
415	// user's pointer to the real registry file, not a partial creation of this
416	// run.
417	func removePartialNewRegistry(path string) {
418		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
419		if err != nil || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
420			return
421		}
422		os.Remove(path)
423	}
424

426		proposal := govflow.Proposal{ID: "gip-7", Title: "fund the audit workstream", State: "voting", Quorum: 1000,
427			TimelockEnd: 5000, Actions: []string{"transfer:audits:25000"}}
428		if err := govflow.Vote(&proposal, 700, true); err != nil {
429			fmt.Println("vote refused:", err)
430		}
431		if err := govflow.Vote(&proposal, 200, false); err != nil {
432			fmt.Println("vote refused:", err)
433		}
434		next := govflow.Tally(&proposal)
435		fmt.Printf("proposal=%s for=%d against=%d quorum=%d next=%s\n", proposal.ID, proposal.ForVotes, proposal.AgainstVotes, proposal.Quorum, next)
436		proposal.State = next
437		proposal.TimelockEnd = 400
438		fmt.Println("executable now:", govflow.Executable([]govflow.Proposal{proposal}, 1000))
439	}

DAO 治理提案与执行平台：长期产品目标

## 产品定位

建设一个 DAO 治理提案与执行平台。产品应以清晰的领域模型和稳定接口承载真实业务增长，在正确性、可审计性、可观测性与运维可控性之间取得平衡，并能在本机离线、可复现地运行。

## 产品范围

- 提案生命周期：草拟、投票、通过、拒绝、执行与撤销。
- 投票与计票：权重、法定人数、委托与声誉。
- 资金库：预算、支出、多签与时间锁执行。
- 执行与回滚：动作序列、失败处理与回滚策略。
- 治理审计：投票、委托与资金变动的完整留痕。

## 核心质量目标

- 计票与法定人数规则确定且可测试，边界情形有明确结论。
- 执行具有幂等性，重复执行不产生二次资金变动。
- 委托与投票权重可追溯，不允许静默覆盖。

## 技术方向

主要技术方向：dao, governance, voting, proposal, multisig, treasury-management, reputation-system。实现以 Go 标准库为主，全部行为可在单机离线环境复现。

## 演进规则

每一轮工作都必须依据当前冻结源码提出真实产品演进，覆盖 feature 迭代、Bug 修复、代码重构、工程化、代码测试、代码理解以及必要的 0-1 子系统建设。
优先选择困难或地狱级任务，强调并发安全、时间语义、幂等性、数据一致性、故障恢复、查询性能、规则冲突、可审计性、兼容迁移与确定性测试等需要系统推理的边界。
不得为凑数重复已有能力、只改文案，或引入与产品价值无关的复杂度；也不得依赖不可用的外部服务或真实链上网络。

## 验收取向

每题都必须具有可独立验收的用户价值：行为可由命令行或测试确定性复现，失败与成功都能被真实观察。
真实产品测试失败须保留原样并给出归因，不要求全部断言通过；环境缺失、未执行与超时不得算作产品缺陷。

content.text:
Done. The duplicated batch-acceptance logic now exists in exactly one place, and every existing test plus end-to-end CLI behavior is preserved.

## What changed

**New file `govflow/batchreg/acceptance.go`** — the single definition of how one already-validated record is accepted:
- `differingFields(existing, in)` — lists mismatches in the fixed **product, quantity, unit** order (replaces the old duplicated `diffFields`, now removed).
- `batchTable` — an append-only working set over a *copy* of the stored records, with `index` (id → record) and `firstPos` (1-based position where this submission first introduced each new id).
- `accept(in, sourcePos)` — the shared rule: unknown id → append, `created=true`; known id with identical content → return the **already-held** record (`created=false`, submitted values can never replace it); known id with different content → return the mismatch list and leave the table untouched.
- `conflictSource(id)` — attributes a conflict: ids stored before the run always resolve to the **registry**; ids introduced this run resolve to their **first** manifest position. Intermediate duplicate confirmations never become a source.

**`govflow/batchreg/batchreg.go`**
- `Register` and `Import` both run their create/duplicate/conflict decision through `batchTable.accept` instead of each carrying their own copy of it.
- Kept entry-point-specific, exactly as required: input validation and its precedence (Register: empty→encoding→quantity; Import: encoding→empty→quantity), the verbatim-vs-trimmed text boundary (normalization still happens only in the CLI/`ParseManifest`, never in the library), the `storedDuplicateID` refusal, Import's all-or-nothing copy/rollback, and the distinct `ConflictError` vs `ManifestConflictError` types with their wording. No registry-file-format change.

**New `acceptance_test.go`** locks in the shared invariants (create / duplicate-echoes-held / conflict-field-order / table untouched on rejection / registry-vs-manifest source / byte-for-byte ids).

## Verified end-to-end (built binary)
- Create → trimmed identical repeat (`duplicate`) → differing submit rejected naming `product, quantity, unit`; stored record survives.
- Task's exact case: new B1 at rec1, identical at rec3, differing qty at rec5 → error points at **record 5 vs manifest record 1**, and no registry file is left behind; with B1 pre-stored the same shape correctly says **registered record**.
- A later invalid record (rec6 blank product) outranks an earlier conflict (validation precedence preserved).
- All-duplicate import leaves file **bytes and mtime unchanged**; save failures still report failure rather than success.

`go vet` clean, `go test -count=1 ./...` green for both packages. The one pre-existing `gofmt` nit in `cmd/govflow/main_import_invalid_first_test.go` predates this work (confirmed with the change stashed) and was left untouched.
